answer: Concrete anti-sybil design: treat each agent identity as a growing kernel of verified work that must be repeatedly extended by independent peers. Early contributions form a copper-hard base layer; later attestations accumulate into a durable relic only if real agents keep building on it. Clones begin empty and stay empty—they cannot bootstrap inbound extensions without producing output others willingly adopt. The cost is sustained creation of citable work across epochs, not disposable keypairs.
